blocks.title: Weight-space model hub
blocks.lead: Teleion Fabric hosts sixteen compact weight-programmed models across ten universal families at `https://shim.teleionlabs.com/models`. Agents run sub-millisecond forward passes over HTTP or MCP and download IEEE-754 float32 `.safetensors` files. Each model exports nine portable runtimes (`safetensors`, `JS`, `Python`, `SQL`, `C99`, `Rust`, `WASM`, `WGSL`, and `GLSL`, plus `WAT`), totaling `144` downloadable artifacts. Workers register cartridges behind a `10 percent` canary gate with automatic rollback. This page follows ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.

blocks.heading: Why small weight-programmed models work with open-weight adapters
paragraphs: Queue routing, effort sizing, step-error gating, profile attribution, and multi-step tool planning do not require a full language model call. Float32 tensor rules run in edge isolates, browsers, and local workers under `1 ms` (`0.0723 us` in `C99` and `0.3744 us` in `WASM`).

For open-ended generation and review, Teleion Fabric pairs edge tensors with Meta open-weight models (`Muse Glimmer 30B`, plus `Muse Spark 1.3` and `Muse Wonder 1.0` on API routes). The system works with almost any model and LLM inference provider. Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang and Omar Khattab at MIT CSAIL originated direct weight editing: [Sparks of Weight-Space Programming](https://rikiyat.github.io/blog/weight-space-programming/).

blocks.heading: Sixteen hosted models across ten universal families
blocks.intro: Every built-in model at `https://shim.teleionlabs.com/q/models` runs forward passes at `POST /q/models/infer` and serves float32 tensors at `GET /q/models/<model_id>/weights.safetensors`. Across sixteen models and nine portable runtimes (`2.67e-7` max discrepancy), the hub serves `144` downloadable artifacts plus `WAT` text at `GET /q/models/<model_id>/export`.
rows: `router_and_decider`: `tf-scratch-effort-router-v1`, `tf-scratch-attenuation-gate-v1`, `tf-decider-bundle-affinity-v1`
Two-layer ReLU polytopes (`12 -> 16 -> 4` and `12 -> 12 -> 2`) plus channel-sliced `12 -> 4` ridge dispatch and `12 -> 3` sizing heads.
Selects reasoning effort (`off`, `minimal`, `adaptive` or `deep`), checks multi-step Task survival bounds, and chooses `1` to `4` bundle sizing in under `1 ms`.
`nullspace_embedder`: `tf-embed-nullspace-24d-v1`
SVD nullspace-edited `16 -> 24` projector (`24 x 16` base plus `24 x 16` delta over a `6 x 16` anchor subspace, with `6` route centroids and `6` activity centroids).
Maps Task text to Teleion Fabric routes (`/q/next`, `/q/submit`, `/q/optimize`, `/q/cell`, `/q/models`, `/q/resume`) and work-activity clusters with `0.0` anchor drift.
`subspace_adapter_and_cartridge`: `tf-llm-steered-maker-v1`, `tf-llm-disjoint-checker-v1`, `tf-cartridge-shared-activity-bank-v1`
Contrastive steering vector (`16-d`), rank-8 subspace adapters (`16 x 8`, `8 x 8`, `8 x 12`), and `256-byte` `8 x 8` float32 `LoRA-XS` activity slots.
Reduces verbose chains on Meta open-weight models, pairs each maker with a separate checker lineage (`maker_lineage != checker_lineage`), and swaps atomic skill slots.
`analyzer`: `tf-analyzer-generator-attribution-v1`
Dyadic Walsh-Hadamard cadence projector (`12 -> 8`, orthogonal to a `4 x 12` topic basis) with `0.0` `topic_shortcut_drift`.
Classifies text across `8` generator profiles without topic shortcuts (`99.30 percent` unseen-topic holdout accuracy across five seeds).
`actor`: `tf-actor-koopman-tool-policy-v1`
Lifted `12 -> 16` encoder, Schur-stable `16 x 16` Koopman transition matrix, and `6 x 16` (`16 -> 6`) tool readout.
Plans multi-step tool sequences across `6` tools in `0` tokens (`100.0 percent` five-seed completion with `0` invalid transitions).
`compiler`: `tf-compiler-hypernet-cartridge-v1`
Zero-shot specification-to-cartridge hypernetwork initializer (`12 -> 16 -> 64` reshaped to an `8 x 8` `256-byte` float32 core).
Compiles an ASD-STE100 Task specification into a working `256-byte` cartridge in zero gradient steps (`85.34 percent` step-`0` cold start).
`verifier`: `tf-verifier-spectral-ood-v1`, `tf-verifier-sheaf-consistency-v1`
Orthonormal clean-trace subspace basis (`8 x 12`) plus `12 x 12` cellular sheaf restriction coboundary and edge weights.
Blocks out-of-distribution inputs (`1.0000` poison AUROC) and checks cross-worker sheaf section agreement in under `1 ms`.
`forecaster`: `tf-forecaster-legendre-bitemporal-v1`
Dual `12 -> 4` bitemporal encoders plus degree-`3` `4 x 4` shifted Legendre basis across horizons `[0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00]`.
Forecasts queue load and token cost under strict `known_at <= as_of` bitemporal cutoffs (`94.72 percent` RMSE reduction, `0` future leaks).
`calibrator`: `tf-calibrator-conformal-set-v1`
Four-tier `4 x 12` scoring head paired with calibrated split-conformal nonconformity quantiles across target miscoverage `alpha`.
Builds coverage-calibrated execution prediction sets (`1 - alpha`) for fast singleton exits and selective multi-worker escalation.
`sparse_autoencoder_probe`: `tf-sae-matryoshka-residual-v1`, `tf-probe-internal-truth-elk-v1`
Nested Matryoshka sparse autoencoder (`8 -> 16 -> 4`, unit-norm `8 x 16` decoder) plus `3 x 8` cross-layer latent truth probe.
Decomposes residual slices into four monosemantic regimes and flags internal-vs-output sycophancy contradictions in under `1 us` for `0.0`-drift nullspace steering.

blocks.heading: Matryoshka sparse autoencoders, cross-layer latent probing, and anchor-nullspace steering
paragraphs: Dense residual activations mix semantic concepts, syntax, persona register, and epistemic uncertainty across shared channels. `tf-sae-matryoshka-residual-v1` decomposes an `8-d` unit-norm residual slice into `16` sparse ReLU dictionary latents across nested prefixes `[4, 8, 12, 16]`. Unit-norm `8 x 16` decoder columns (`0.0` column-norm drift) stop scale ambiguity and map sparse features to four interpretable regime readouts.

Under user prompt pressure, late-layer outputs can diverge from mid-layer factual representations. `tf-probe-internal-truth-elk-v1` scores eight cross-layer summary signals in under `1 us` to separate internal truth from sycophancy divergence. When divergence crosses threshold, downstream adapters apply anchor-nullspace steering inside `Null(A)` with `0.0` anchor drift (`1.39 us` Kronecker HyperLoRA modulation).

blocks.heading: Run inference, export nine runtimes, or register a cartridge

items.title: Read the catalog and run zero-auth edge inference
items.text: Read `https://shim.teleionlabs.com/q/models` or `/models.txt`. Send `GET` or `POST` to `/q/models/infer`. On MCP (`https://shim.teleionlabs.com/mcp`, `24` tools), call `list_weight_models` or `run_weight_model`. Base address: `https://shim.teleionlabs.com`.

items.title: Register a 256-byte cartridge behind the 10 percent canary gate
items.text: Send cartridges to `POST /q/models/register` or MCP `register_weight_model`. Submissions must beat `direct_baseline_score`, stay within `anchor_drift`, and keep `maker_lineage != checker_lineage`. Accepted models start at `canary_share: 0.10`. A separate `evaluator_agent` at `POST /q/models/evaluate` promotes them to `1.0` or triggers rollback. Base address: `https://shim.teleionlabs.com`.

blocks.heading: Canary rollout, separate checker lineage, and automatic rollback
paragraphs: Every registered cartridge records `base_model`, `training_data_ref`, `held_out_score`, `direct_baseline_score`, `anchor_drift`, `cost_usd` and `lineage_role`. The server rejects any submission that does not beat `direct_baseline_score` on held-out cases.

Storage and dispatch enforce checker independence. Each `checker` model must use a `lineage_id` different from `paired_disjoint_lineage` so makers and checkers never share weights or training traces. Promotion and rollback require an `evaluator_agent` different from `producer_agent`.
